regression_power.rationale: With zero tests, any refactor of the data layer (the most likely future change) can silently break pagination, sorting, form exclusion, or freshness and only the external acceptance suite would notice — if it's still run.

evidence: app/ — no test files at all, so no low-value tests either (facts: tests.cases 0)
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, per the rubric's neutral score for an empty suite; the cost is entirely in the missing signal.

findings.issue: The home-list filter/pagination pipeline (combined q+type+generation filtering, page clamping, 48-item slicing) has no tests; this is the code most likely to be refactored and most likely to regress subtly.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests with a stubbed fetch (everything funnels through api() at :34): counts for each filter and combinations, page out-of-range clamping, boundary pages with exactly 0/1/48/49 matches.

findings.issue: cardsFor — species mapping, dedup by id, and alternate-form exclusion (id >= 10000) is unguarded; a regression leaks Mega forms into every card list or links to the wrong species.
findings.suggestion: Test cardsFor directly with fixture refs including IDs above 10000, duplicates, and references whose species differs from the pokemon name (deoxys-normal).

findings.issue: Sort comparator: missing-values-last in both directions, numeric vs string comparison, label tie-break, and aria-sort reset are unverified; a refactor could sort '10' before '9' or drop nulls to the top.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator and unit-test it: nulls last ascending and descending, numeric columns, string columns, tie-break stability.

findings.issue: The hand-rolled TTL cache (in-flight dedup, error eviction at :50, sweep every 500 writes) is untested; a broken eviction serves stale data for up to 60s — the exact bug class the spec's live-data-overlay scenario guards against.
findings.suggestion: Test hit/miss/expiry/retry-after-error behaviour with fake timers, or replace with a small vetted caching library to shrink the untested surface.

findings.issue: URL-state plumbing — the debounce race (the q-sync effect at :36-42 skips syncing while a timer is pending) and pageHref's default-omission logic at :62 are untested.
findings.suggestion: A couple of Playwright component/route tests: back-navigation during a pending debounce, changing a filter resets page to 1, empty/default params are omitted from generated hrefs.

findings.issue: pokemonMoves — method ordering (level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical), the 'method|move|level' dedup key, and per-table default ordering are untested.
findings.suggestion: Fixture-based unit test on a small synthetic moves payload covering method order, dedup of repeated version_group_details, and level-then-name ordering.

findings.issue: Pure helpers (humanize, dexNumber, show, pageTitle) — the cheapest tests in the codebase — are absent; these encode spec-critical rules like 'Mr Mime' and '#0025'.
findings.suggestion: A five-minute unit file covering hyphen edge cases ('mr-mime', 'ho-oh'), zero-padding, and null → em dash.

findings.issue: English-entry selection and fallbacks (englishName, latestEnglish, collapse whitespace, move effect fallback to flavor text at :319-323) are untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with multi-language fixture entries asserting the English name, the last English flavor text, and the short_effect→flavor→em-dash fallback chain.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrder maps null 404 records to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and pokemonMoves depends on game sort order for the default selection ([name].tsx:60); neither edge is tested.
findings.suggestion: Test ordering with a missing version group and assert the default game is the highest-order one.

findings.issue: No test script, runner, or devDependency wired up, so future contributors have no way to run any test even if they add one.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest as a devDependency with a 'test' script and a couple of tests for lib/ pure logic as a starting point.

summary: The app shipped with zero tests of its own: no runner, no script, no test files. Yet it contains a substantial hand-rolled data layer — filtering, pagination, sorting, species/form mapping, and a custom cache — that is precisely the code that regresses silently under refactor. The acceptance suite was given, not written, and once it stops being the only guard nothing here would catch a broken data layer.
